stem.en: Why does the writer mention the day after tomorrow?

options.en: To show that a missing word does not mean a missing idea
To show that lists of untranslatable words are often inaccurate
To give an example of an English word that has no translation
To suggest that English speakers think less precisely about time

why.en: English has no everyday single word for the day after tomorrow, yet its speakers understand the idea perfectly well: a missing word is not a missing idea. The writer is not sceptical of the lists themselves, the example is of a word English lacks, and nobody is said to be confused about time.
why.uz: Ingliz tilida 'indinga' uchun kundalik bitta soʻz yoʻq, ammo bu tilda soʻzlashuvchilar bu tushunchani yaxshi tushunadi: soʻzning yoʻqligi gʻoyaning yoʻqligini anglatmaydi. Muallif roʻyxatlarning oʻziga shubha bilan qaramaydi, misol ingliz tilida yoʻq soʻz haqida, vaqtni chalkashtirish haqida esa hech kim gapirmaydi.
why.ru: В английском нет обиходного отдельного слова для «послезавтра», но носители прекрасно понимают это понятие: отсутствие слова не означает отсутствия идеи. Сами списки автор не ставит под сомнение, пример касается слова, которого в английском нет, и никто не говорит, что носители путаются во времени.

stem.en: What does the writer suggest learners should do when they meet a word with no neat equivalent?

options.en: Treat it as a window into what its speakers care about
Treat it as proof that its speakers see the world differently
Find out when and why the word first entered the language
Learn it as part of a list of words that cannot be translated

why.en: The writer calls such a word 'an invitation: a small window into what other people have repeatedly found worth talking about'. That speakers of other languages see the world in ways others cannot reach is the message the writer doubts, and the writer suggests neither researching the word's history nor learning lists.
why.uz: Muallif bunday soʻzni 'taklif: boshqalar qayta-qayta gapirishga arziydi deb topgan narsaga ochilgan kichik deraza' deb ataydi. Boshqa til egalari dunyoni boshqalar yeta olmaydigan tarzda koʻradi degan fikrga muallif shubha bilan qaraydi, soʻz tarixini oʻrganish yoki roʻyxatlarni yodlashni esa taklif qilmaydi.
why.ru: Автор называет такое слово «приглашением: небольшим окном в то, о чём другие люди снова и снова считали нужным говорить». Мысль о том, что носители других языков видят мир недоступным для остальных образом, автор как раз ставит под сомнение, а изучать историю слова или учить списки не предлагает.

stem.en: Why did the neighbour's question change Gulnora's thinking?

options.en: It showed that none of them knew the orchard as a working place.
It showed that only Dilbar, who visited often, really knew the trees.
It showed that the harvest would need more workers than the family had.
It showed that the neighbour could run the orchard without the family.

why.en: Gulnora realised she did not know how many trees there were, which fruited first or where the ladders were kept, and she suspected her brother and sister could not answer either. Dilbar 'had loved' the orchard but is not said to know it, and the number of workers or the neighbour running it is never raised.
why.uz: Gulnora daraxtlar nechta ekanini, qaysi biri birinchi meva berishini va narvonlar qayerda turishini bilmasligini angladi, akasi va singlisi ham javob bera olmasligiga shubha qildi. Dilbar bogʻni sevgan, lekin uni yaxshi bilgani aytilmagan; ishchilar soni yoki bogʻni qoʻshni yuritishi haqida gap yoʻq.
why.ru: Гульнора поняла, что не знает, сколько там деревьев, какие плодоносят первыми и где хранятся лестницы, и заподозрила, что брат и сестра тоже не ответили бы. Дильбар сад «любила», но не сказано, что она его знала; о нехватке работников или о том, что сосед мог бы вести сад сам, речи нет.

stem.en: Why was the photograph strong evidence?

options.en: It showed that people already used one particular route.
It showed that the old path was too narrow for so many walkers.
It showed that the ground was too wet for paths in winter.
It showed that the lot was too small for both paths and a fountain.

why.en: After a light snowfall only the old path showed, as 'a single dark line', while 'every other part of the lot lay untouched': people really walked along that one line. The photo was not about the path's width, wet ground or the size of the lot.
why.uz: Yengil qordan keyin faqat eski soʻqmoq yagona qora chiziq boʻlib koʻrinardi, maydonning qolgan hamma joyi esa bosilmagan edi: odamlar haqiqatan ham aynan shu chiziq boʻylab yurardi. Surat soʻqmoqning kengligi, nam yer yoki maydon oʻlchami haqida emas edi.
why.ru: После лёгкого снегопада старая тропинка была видна как «одна тёмная линия», а «вся остальная часть участка оставалась нетронутой»: люди действительно ходили именно по этой линии. Фотография не говорила ни о ширине тропинки, ни о мокрой земле, ни о размерах участка.

stem.en: What is the main point of the final paragraph?

options.en: How a place is really used is useful knowledge that is easy to overlook.
The students knew the planners' name for such paths and used it well.

why.en: The final paragraph says a place 'carries information about how it is actually used' that is easy to overlook because nobody writes it down. It says the students did not need the planners' name for such paths, and it makes no general claim about unplanned paths or about architects.
